payload.headline: Netflix near fair value: cash strong, growth slowing, chart weak; wait for 61

summary.thesis: Netflix is a solid, cash-rich business priced about at fair value (base DCF 65.31 vs price 64.54), so there is no safety margin while growth slows and analysts trim estimates.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait for the downtrend to break.

payload.happening: NFLX closed at 64.54, up 2.02% on the day, but it is still in a downtrend below its falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (65.25, 70.0 and 80.71). Intraday it trades at 63.24 (not a close), giving back part of that gain just under resistance at 64.84–65.32. There is no news since the last note. The next scheduled event is earnings on 2027-01-19, and analysts have cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% over the last 30 days.
payload.business: Some changes affect the business itself. Sales growth is slowing: quarterly revenue growth fell from 16.19% two quarters ago to 11.85% now, against 14.65% for the trailing year. Profitability is improving: operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 11.4B from 9.0B. The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share owns more of the company. The balance sheet is not a worry. Debt is 12.7B against 8.2B of cash (net cash -4.4B), which is small next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. Two things are at risk. First, the growth rate. Second, the margin, which the filings flag as at the top of its 5-year range (17–31%), and peaks like that usually fade. Other changes move mainly sentiment and governance: small analyst estimate cuts (-1.11% over 30 days), the weak chart, and 3 new risk headings in the annual report, which the data calls not alarming on its own. Our data has no segment breakdown, so competition can't be measured here. Streaming competition is a standing issue (general knowledge).

worth.text: On earnings the stock costs 18.3 times trailing EPS and 17.1 times next year's estimate. It trades at 5.3 times sales, below the peer median of 7.2 and at the 25th percentile of its own 5-year range, so it looks cheap against peers and its own history. A cash-flow model (DCF) tells a more modest story. The base case gives 65.31, almost exactly today's price. Put another way, the current price assumes free cash flow starts out growing about 14.4% a year, in line with the 15% sales growth of recent years. The methods disagree mainly because of the growth assumption. At 10% starting growth the value is 54.07, and at 20% it is 80.74. The DCF bear case of 38.33 uses analysts' 5% next-year EPS growth. The own-history range (60.37–122.15) assumes the market goes back to paying past sales multiples. Margins matter too: if the operating margin fell to 23%, the value drops to 60.29. My fair-value range is 54.07–80.74, centred near the 65.31 base, so today's price offers no real discount.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow keeps growing at roughly the 14.4% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has already slowed to 11.85%.

bull: Cash generation is strong and rising: free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, a 22.87% free-cash-flow margin.
It is cheap versus peers and its own past: price/sales of 5.3 vs a peer median of 7.2, at the 25th percentile of its 5-year range.
Buybacks shrink the share count (-3.35% a year), and if growth holds near 20% the DCF value is 80.74.
bear: Growth is decelerating: quarterly revenue growth fell to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
The 31.3% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range, and a fall to 23% would cut value to 60.29.
Analysts are cutting: this quarter's EPS estimate is down 7.3% in 30 days (0.73 to 0.68), and the price is below a falling 200-day average of 80.71.

levels.what: DCF base value; at the 64.54 close the stock is at fair value with no margin of safety
Bottom of the 61.15–61.63 support zone, a first area to start buying
Low end of its own-history price/sales range, close to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (37561)

longterm.why: The business is good (grade B), but the price sits right at the base fair value while growth and estimates are slipping. A move into the low 60s would add a margin of safety.

swing.why: The trend is down, the stock is pressing resistance at 64.84–65.32 and slipped to 63.24 intraday, and the next resistance (66.54–67.49) is closer than support (61.15–61.63) is below. Wait for a close above 65.32, which also reclaims the 20-day average of 65.25.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-19 come after the 2027-01-15 options expiry. That options price already reflects a move of about 11.7% before the report, and falling estimates make a cautious entry ahead of it sensible.

change_mind: Next quarter's report shows revenue growth back above 11.85% and revenue at or above the 13.4B consensus, with operating margin holding near 31.3%. That would support the 80.74 high end.
A daily close above 67.49 (top of the upper resistance zone) would end the lower-highs pattern and turn the swing view to enter.
A close below 61.15, or operating margin falling back under 29.14%, would point toward the 54.07 low end and delay any buying.
